text.p: Salomon Brothers said on Wednesday it rated Swedish automotive group AB Volvo as a "buy" and Swedish truck maker Scania AB as "underperform".

"In Sweden we expect the turnaround in core businesses to lift Volvo, but we expect the slow letdown of expectations at Scania to continue," said Salomon Brothers analyst John Lawson in an analysis called European Auto Digest.
He gave Volvo a "buy" with a share price target of 195 crowns, while he rated Scania "underperform" and "vulnerable to disappointment above 160 crowns".
At the close on Wednesday Volvo was trading at 183 crowns and Scania at 191.5 crowns.
A Salomon Brothers spokeswoman said the ratings had not been changed recently, but in the report Lawson said Volvo's share price target was lifted.
"We have raised our share price target in line with the big run-up in the Swedish market and a slightly higher earnings estimate for 1997," he said.
"We have warmed to Volvo because we believe the trends in the core businesses are currently running more positively and may report improving performances over the next few quarters," Lawson said.
Regarding Volvo's large surplus cash, he forecast that some of it could well be distributed ahead of any change in the share buy-back regulations in Sweden.
Currently, companies are not allowed to buy back their own shares, but authorities are looking into the regulations and investors expect Volvo to buy back shares when it becomes allowed.
Salomon Brothers expected Volvo to post 1996 earnings per share of 8.60 crowns. In 1997, it saw EPS of 12.10 crowns and in 1998 at 15.30 crowns.

"The value key is the forward earnings potential in a very competitive market place," he said. "We do not believe that the (new) 4-Series will fully replicate the stature of the outgoing 3-Series and, as a result, rebuild all of the tremendous profitability previously enjoyed by the company."
"The stock has performed poorly against the Swedish market, but notwithstanding an appetite for cyclicals, the ratings remain extremely high and vulnerable to disappointment above 160 crowns."
Salomon Brothers forecast Scania will post 1996 earnings per share of 9.40 crowns. In 1997, it expects the company's EPS to amount to 12.60 crowns and in 1998 to 13.30 crowns.
